issue.title: Distinguish pre-watch failures from confirmed build failures in --format jsonl

repository.name: NodeKit
repository.description: Admin tool authoring client for genomic analysis pipeline (C# / Avalonia)

issue.body:
## Summary
External review follow-up on #85 (P3): a connection failure reported the same `error_code: "BUILD_FAILED"` as a genuine NodeVault-side build failure — repro was `--url http://127.0.0.1:1` yielding `{"error_code":"BUILD_FAILED","message":"NodeVault에 연결할 수 없습니다..."}`, indistinguishable from a real build failure without parsing `message`.

## Fix
Uses a signal `SubmitCommand` already tracks — whether a build ID has been received — rather than guessing from the error message string (explicitly rejected: `BuildEvent.Message` is human text, and the underlying gRPC `StatusCode` isn't preserved past `GrpcToolSpecClient`'s catch blocks).

- Build ID known (failure came from `WatchToolBuild` itself) → `error_code: "BUILD_FAILED"`, `phase: "watch"`, `remote_build_state: "failed"` — a **confirmed** remote outcome.
- No build ID ever received (failure came from `ResolveToolSpec`/`SubmitToolBuild`) → `error_code: "PRE_WATCH_FAILED"`, `phase: "pre_watch"`, `remote_build_state: "unknown"`. Deliberately does **not** claim the remote build wasn't created — `SubmitToolBuild` could have succeeded server-side with only its response lost, in which case NodeVault may already be building. `"unknown"` is the honest answer.

`request_id` (for idempotent retry/status-check) was **not** added this round — it needs `GrpcToolSpecClient` to surface the `SubmitToolBuild` idempotency key it already generates internally, which is the same class of `BuildEvent`/client-contract change as preserving gRPC status codes for finer-grained pre-watch error codes. Filed together as #86.

Human-mode output and all exit codes are unchanged — this only affects `--format jsonl`'s `completed` record.

## Validation run
- `dotnet build`: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `dotnet test`: 709 total, 707 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (opt-in NodeVault integration)
- `dotnet format NodeKit.sln --verify-no-changes`: clean
- New tests: resolve-stage connection failure → `PRE_WATCH_FAILED`, submit-stage RPC failure → `PRE_WATCH_FAILED`, `WatchToolBuild` terminal failure → `BUILD_FAILED`, pre-watch failure message doesn't assert "remote build wasn't created", human output/exit codes unchanged, jsonl stdout stays pure JSON

issue.title: feat(grpc): P05.wire staged ToolSpec client seam + S2-01 wire proofs

repository.name: NodeKit
repository.description: Admin tool authoring client for genomic analysis pipeline (C# / Avalonia)

issue.body:
## P05.wire:W — ToolSpec real client wire contract (NodeKit v0.9.1 S2-01)

Task `OP-NODEKIT-CLI-P05-20261008` / stage `P05.wire:W`, base main `0241db8f6e309b84891df6008fc5ace5cee44d55`.
Writer: Operator session `032faefa-eb84-4a4a-86dc-15db7fefe22e`.

### What changes
- **Staged client seam on the shared `IToolSpecBuildClient`:** `ToolSpecBuildOptions` adds `RequestId`, a caller-provided identity, and `BeforeSubmitAsync`, a durable-store seam. The client awaits the seam after `ResolveToolSpec` and before `SubmitToolBuild`.
  - If the store throws (anything other than a cancellation), there is no Submit and no Watch. The run ends with a `Failed` event that names the request ID.
  - Cancellation still propagates.
  - The request ID sent on the wire is always the stored ID.
- **Full resolved basis:** `ToolSpecSubmitBasis` holds the requested name, version and `requested_at`, plus the server's `tool_spec_digest`, `tool_name`, `version` and `resolved_at`. It rides on the spec-resolved `BuildEvent.SubmitBasis`, so no caller has to parse the shortened log line. `JobCreated` now carries `RequestId`.
- **Compatibility:** the existing 4-arg `ResolveAndBuildAsync` stays as an adapter: it uses default options and a fresh GUID per submit, so GUI and CLI behaviour is unchanged. The new overload has a default interface implementation for existing implementers (GUI and test fakes). It delegates only when the options are empty, and throws `NotSupportedException` otherwise, so options are never silently ignored.
- `FakeBuildService` records each deserialized Resolve, Submit and Watch request and the RPC order.

### S2-01 evidence map (`tests/NodeKit.Cli.Tests/ToolSpecWireP05Tests.cs`)
| ID | Test(s) | Layer |
|---|---|---|
| C01 | `S2_01_C01_MissingSourceChecksum_ExitsOneWithZeroRpc`, `…VersionOnlyPackage_StrictReproducible_ExitsOneWithZeroRpc`, `…VersionOnlyPackage_DefaultSubmit_SendsTheRenderedPayloadUnchanged` | `SubmitCommand` + real `GrpcToolSpecClient` → in-process gRPC |
| C02 | `S2_01_C02_ResolveRequest_CarriesRecipeIdentityAndRenderedRawSpecBytes` (raw_spec == `render --format raw-spec` bytes, exactly 7 keys in order, `requested_at` in ms), `…IsNotTheLegacyBuildRequestPreview` | generated gRPC request capture |
| C03 | `S2_01_C03_ResolvedDigestAndBuildId_FlowIntoSubmitAndWatch_InOrderOnceEach` | gRPC sequence capture |
| C04 | `S2_01_C04_ResolveUnavailable_NoSubmitNoWatch_FailedWithDiagnostic`, `…CliReportsPreWatchUnknown_WithoutRetry` | transport error fixture |
| C05 | `S2_01_C05_SubmitResponseLost_NoWatch_NoBuildIdInvented`, `…CliKeepsRemoteStateUnknown` | transport fault fixture |
| C06 | class summary + `FakeBuildService` comment: the fake does not parse raw_spec, does not enforce DisallowUnknownFields or full pins, does not dedup on the server side, and does not check registry existence. Live integration (`GrpcToolSpecClientIntegrationTests`) is not run here and is out of scope. | source/evidence review |

Staged seam tests: the caller request ID becomes the Submit request ID and appears on `JobCreated`; the store sees the full basis before any Submit (Submit count 0 at store time); a store failure means Submit and Watch are 0; a store cancellation propagates; the default overload sends a fresh GUID each time; a blank request ID is rejected before any RPC; a legacy-only implementer delegates on default options and throws `NotSupportedException` otherwise.

### Verification (seoy, .NET 10.0.201, Release)
- **Old-red:** the new tests on the unchanged base source fail to compile with 20 errors (CS0246 `ToolSpecBuildOptions` / `ToolSpecSubmitBasis`).
- **Green:** full solution build had 0 warnings and 0 errors. `ToolSpecWireP05Tests` + `GrpcToolSpecClient*` + `SubmitCommandTests`: 132 total, 0 failed, 1 skipped (the live NodeVault integration test, which needs `NODEKIT_NODEVAULT_URL`).
- **Mutations** (each build confirmed at 0 errors before the run):
  - m1 sends a fresh GUID as the Submit request ID → 2/18 fail (CallerRequestId, BeforeSubmit basis).
  - m2 swallows the store failure → 1/18 fails (BeforeSubmitFails).
- Local `/tmp` tree and seoy tree hashes match (`e61f63d8`).
- Format check, the strict `TreatWarningsAsErrors` build and the full suites: see the follow-up comment / CI.

### Boundaries
- This adds no journal or receipt storage. P04.store/integrate consumes this seam, and the order P05.wire → P04 → P05.reentry/result is unchanged.
- #86: no `FailurePhase`/`GrpcStatusCode`/`FailureKind` and no server request_id lookup were added. A submit with no build_id stays unknown, and nothing resubmits automatically.
- #74 (heartbeat/reconnect/replay) and #59 (real NodeVault submit) remain later integration work. The local fake passing is not evidence of a real server.
- There is no new GUI feature; the GUI caller compiles unchanged.

issue.title: feat(cli): durable local operation journal and receipt (P04.store, S2-02)

repository.name: NodeKit
repository.description: Admin tool authoring client for genomic analysis pipeline (C# / Avalonia)

issue.body:
## P04.store:W — durable local operation journal and receipt (S2-02)

NodeKit v0.9.1 contract stage **P04.store:W**: the shared durable request identity and receipt foundation (S2-02-C01..C08). It sits on the P05.wire seam (`ToolSpecBuildOptions.RequestId` / `BeforeSubmitAsync`), which landed in #117.

### What this adds (`src/NodeKit.Cli/Operations/`)
- **Record layout:** `LocalOperationStore` keeps its record root at `.nodekit` next to the Recipe by default. Inside it:
  - `receipts/<request-id>.json` is the mutable operation receipt.
  - `snapshots/source/<sha256>.json` holds the exact authoring and companion bytes. It is immutable and content-addressed.
  - `snapshots/resolved/<sha256>.json` holds the actual ResolveToolSpec return, bound to the source snapshot and the envelope. It is also immutable and content-addressed.
- **Receipt schema `nodekit.operation.v1`:**
  - Fixed when the receipt is created: `operation_kind`, `request_id`, `endpoint`, the exact `envelope` (tool_name/version/raw_spec) plus `envelope_sha256`, and `source_snapshot_sha256`.
  - Only these move forward: `phase` (prepared → submit_in_flight → acknowledged → terminal), `resolved_snapshot_sha256`, `build_id` and `last_observation`.
- **Writes:** every write goes through the existing `AtomicFileWriter` (same-directory temp file → flush → rename).
- **Locking:** an `OperationHandle` holds a per-receipt writer lock (`.<file>.nodekit-oplock`) for the life of the operation. A second writer gets `OPERATION_LOCKED`/2.
- **`ToolSpecOperationRunner` order:**
  1. The prepared record is written before Resolve.
  2. The resolved snapshot and submit_in_flight are written before Submit, which uses the stored request ID.
  3. build_id is written as acknowledged.
  4. The terminal observation is written.
  - A store failure blocks the next side-effecting RPC.
  - A build_id or result that was observed but couldn't be saved is returned as a diagnostic, exit 2. It is never claimed as durable.
  - A submit_in_flight record without a build_id is refused (`OPERATION_NOT_RESUMABLE`/2, RPC 0). It is never blindly resubmitted.

### S2-02 map (`tests/NodeKit.Cli.Tests/LocalOperationStoreTests.cs`, real generated gRPC fake)
- **C01:** the receipt is `prepared` on disk when Resolve arrives, and `submit_in_flight` with the resolved snapshot when Submit arrives. Submit `request_id` equals the stored fixed ID `1111…`. The source→resolved local binding is checked against the exact bytes.
- **C02:** build_id and the terminal outcome, image digest/ref and health can be read by a fresh store after the handle is closed.
- **C03:** if the prepared write fails, there are 0 RPCs and no record. If the in-flight receipt or resolved-snapshot write fails, Resolve ran but Submit did not, and `ResolveCompleted` tells the two cases apart.
- **C04:** a second run on the same prepared journal reuses the stored ID and payload and redoes the in-flight transition. No new GUID is created.
- **C05:**
  - A changed payload, endpoint, kind or version under the stored ID gives `OPERATION_RECORD_MISMATCH`/2, and the file is unchanged byte-for-byte.
  - Creating over an existing record gives `OPERATION_RECORD_EXISTS`/2.
  - After the Recipe is edited, the change is reported as divergence and the old snapshot bytes are preserved. A replay sends the stored envelope and does not reread the file. A fresh preparation gets a new snapshot.
- **C06:** a concurrent second writer is locked out with 0 RPCs. The holder's own writes are not blocked.
- **C07:** an interrupted replace leaves the previous complete record and no temp files. Six kinds of corrupt record give `OPERATION_RECORD_INVALID`/2 with 0 RPCs: truncated, unsupported schema, envelope hash mismatch, missing snapshot, in-flight without resolved, unknown field. An in-flight record without a build_id is not resubmitted.
- **C08:** if the ack or terminal write fails, exit is 2 and the observed build_id/result appears in the diagnostic. The durable phase stays at the previous step. There is no new Submit and no CancelToolBuild.

### Evidence (seoy, fresh clone at this head)
- **Strict build:** `dotnet build NodeKit.sln -c Release /p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=true /p:EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true` → 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- **New class:** 22/22 pass.
- **NodeKit.Tests:** 501/501.
- **NodeKit.Cli.Tests:** 634 total = 612 base + 22 new, 2 skipped, 1 failure. The failure is `HarborBaseImageSelectionTests.Step4_*`, the seoy environment flake already reproduced on unchanged base in P05. It passed 2/2 when that class was re-run alone. This change does not touch Harbor code.
- **Mutations:** each was built and run against the new class, and each was killed. Sources were restored afterwards.

  | Mutant | Failing tests |
  |---|---|
  | m1: no in-flight record before Submit | 9/22 |
  | m2: operation lock not exclusive | 1 |
  | m3: envelope change allowed | 1 |
  | m4: ack-write failure ignored | 1 |
  | m5: in-flight record resubmitted | 1 |
- **Old-red:** the new tests cannot compile on base `42290e88` because the types don't exist yet.

### Boundaries
- **Store and runner foundation only.** The `--receipt` CLI option, the `SubmitCommand`/function-recipe caller wiring and human/JSONL output belong to **P04.integrate:W**. `receipt watch|cancel|replay` belongs to P05.reentry. `SubmitCommand` behaviour is unchanged.
- **Not claimed:** server-side duplicate prevention, server request_id lookup, #86 detailed failure fields, power-loss durability, or support for every filesystem.
- The local SHA256 binding is a local convention. It is not a global ToolSpec/Manifest/Lock identity.
- The writer does not merge.
